agent_notes: The Hebrew verse 1 is the whole superscription (KJV 57:0). Its terms (lamnatseach, al-tashchet, miktam) are of uncertain meaning; I translated al-tashchet as 'Do not destroy', the sense every version and Rashi/Meiri take, and left miktam transliterated. The historical note (the cave) is the title's own claim; Rashi, Radak and Meiri tie it to 1 Sam 24.

Reviewer request applied: the note on 'peoples ... nations' now separates the three views. Radak takes both words as the families of Israel; Ibn Ezra takes 'peoples' as the many of Israel and 'nations' as non-Israelites; Malbim takes them as nations that have a religion. The KJV 'people' (singular) against the Hebrew plural is kept in the commentary. Pos 5 is the written form with the (V) marker in the packet; the gloss is the same either way.

agent_notes: Verse 5 is syntactically knotted. 'Lions' (levaim) is a rare form of lavi; lohatim is read either as a noun 'blazing ones' in apposition, or as an adjective for 'sons of man', or as 'among' by ellipsis (Ibn Ezra, Meiri, Rashi). KJV/ASV 'set on fire' takes it passively; I took it as active 'those who blaze/devour' (Metzudat Zion links to lahat 'flame'). Rashi's identification of the lions as Abner and Amasa, and Meiri's midrash, are not in the text and I kept them out of the translation.

The subject of kafaf ('bent down') is ambiguous: 'it [the net] bowed my soul', 'each one bent my soul' (Ibn Ezra), or 'my soul is bowed' (KJV/ASV, taking nafshi as subject). I kept the Hebrew order and ambiguity in the literal layer. The perfect 'they have fallen' may be prophetic perfect (Radak, Rashi, Metzudat Zion); I left it as past in the literal layer and mention the reading in the commentary.

Radak glosses 'elohim' as a vocative; all five English versions agree and so do I. 'Steadfast' for nakhon: KJV/ASV 'fixed', YLT 'prepared'; the root kun covers both firm and ready, so I used 'steadfast' in the literal layer and 'steady' in the dramatic.

'My glory' (kevodi) is the soul or the tongue/liver by parallelism; Metzudat Zion and Meiri say it is the soul. KJV 'I myself will awake early' hides the transitive verb: Hebrew has 'I will awaken the dawn' (Rashi, Berakhot 3b). The Targum instead has 'I will rouse myself to praise at the time of dawn'.
